intro_html: The messy sandwich you grew up on, turned into a tidy bowl over crispy potatoes. Each serving carries 46 grams of protein for about $5.86 (at everyday cost). Fourteen servings means the whole family or the whole week is handled.
cost_closing_html: About $5.86 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: Each of the 14 bowls delivers 46 grams of protein and about 681 calories.
upsell_html: It is nostalgic, it is filling, and it will make you the hero of the lunch line. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: The 7 lb ground turkey pack keeps your protein cost down, so buy the big size.
Buy frozen fries by the bag for the base. They are cheaper and last longer than fresh potatoes you cut yourself.
Honey and Dijon are one-bottle buys that last for months, so the cost per batch is basically nothing.
make_it: Bake the fries according to the bag while you get the meat going.
Brown the ground turkey in a large skillet, then add the chopped onion, peppers, and shredded carrots.
Stir in the tomato paste, honey, and honey Dijon mustard to build that sweet-tangy sloppy joe sauce.
Add a splash of water if it gets too thick and simmer until the veggies are tender.
Spoon the sloppy joe mix right over the baked fries and dig in.
